newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks likely to hover narrowly.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks likely to hover narrowly.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to hover narrowly on Friday as selling pressure from position squaring ahead of the weekend will cap gains, brokers said. They added however that fundamentals were sound and bargain-hunting was expected to support the market.
On Thursday, the 225-share Nikkei average lost 39.11 points or 0.19 percent to finish at 20,312.23. June Nikkei futures fell 90 points to 20,310.
"Turnover has been rather feeble and today should be no exception as it is before the weekend," a market analyst at a second-tier brokerage said.

Brokers said a television report on Friday that Tokyo prosecutors had arrested former Nomura Securities Co Ltd president Hideo Sakamaki in connection with a scandal involving allegedly illegal payoffs to a racketeer could have a negative effect on the brokerage's share price. But they speculated that the effect was likely to be limited to Nomura and would not drag down the entire market.

"There is a chance that the shares will buckle and test the low of 1,100 yen achieved after the scandal broke," a broker at a "Big Four" brokerage said. "But the arrest was expected and the market should be fairly immune to the news."

Sakamaki, who stepped down as president in March and is now an adviser to the giant brokerage, told a parliamentary panel this week that he had briefly met the corporate racketeer at the heart of the scandal in 1992, but denied knowledge of any stock deals by the racketeer through Nomura.
